intro: The documents that ship with grooph, rendered for reading. Each page is a file in the repository, linked at its foot.

entries.summary: Open the app and draw, start from a template, install the command line, or ask an agent to draw for you.
For an agent, or a person working with one: when a diagram is needed, the shortest path to one, the tools, and what works in a chat app.
What an agent looks things up in: the smallest document worth drawing, every operation by example, and what to do about each rule.
The graph document: its fields, what they mean, and the rules it must follow.
The second kind of document, for work that spans sessions, people, and accounts.
Templates, registries, and the pattern library, and how to use or save one.
Proposal sets, share links, and the compare view: how an agent offers a few diagrams and a person picks one.
Pictures, the outline, the offline page, embeds, the 3D views, and the six themes.
Every rule by its stable code, with a document that fires it and one that does not.
The command line, command by command, each with the help it prints itself.
All twenty templates as shapes, with when to use each.
Diagrams other people have sent in by pull request, each checked and drawn by CI.
Watching a session: the hook that records which subagents start and stop, and the live view that draws them.
The lab: compiling a diagram into a prompt package, run folders, and the comparison runners, kept in the repository and out of the package.
What the experiments found: the paired comparisons of a compiled diagram against a plain prompt, the check that watching does not interfere, and what each cost.
No account, no server, no cookies, no analytics: where a diagram lives and what leaves your device.
What grooph does with a document someone else made: link limits, size caps, escaping, the offline page, and embeds.
How grooph is built: one pure core and the app, the command line, and the MCP server around it, and why it draws and does not direct.
How to send a diagram, a fix, or a rule, and what a pull request is held to.
Each version, its date, and what changed for a person using it.
